ideas.children_he: רָחֵל הִצְטַעֲרָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ יְלָדִים וְחִפְּשָׂה דֶּרֶךְ לְהָקִים מִשְׁפָּחָה.
ideas.children_en: Rachel wanted children like Leah, so she gave her servant Bilhah to Jacob. Bilhah had two sons for her. Rachel treated these boys as her own sons.

ideas.children_he: גַּם לֵאָה רָצְתָה לְהַרְחִיב אֶת מִשְׁפַּחְתָּהּ.
ideas.children_en: Leah gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob when she could not have children. Zilpah had two sons, named Gad and Asher, making Leah happy.

ideas.children_he: הַמְּרִיבָה בֵּין הָאֲחָיוֹת הִרְאֲתָה כַּמָּה קִנְאָה יְכוֹלָה לְסַבֵּךְ קְשָׁרִים.
ideas.children_en: Leah’s son Reuben brought mandrakes to his mother. Rachel wanted them, so they agreed Rachel would have Jacob that night in exchange for the mandrakes.
Leah had more children for Jacob: Issachar, Zebulun, and a daughter Dinah. She said God gave her a reward because she let her servant be with Jacob.

ideas.children_he: רָחֵל יָלְדָה אֶת יוֹסֵף אַחֲרֵי הַמְתָּנָה אֲרֻכָּה.
ideas.children_en: After praying hard, Rachel had a son named Joseph. She was glad God took away her shame from not having children before.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב רָצָה לַחֲזֹר הַבַּיְתָה עִם מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Jacob asked Laban to let him go home with his wives and children. Laban wanted him to stay, because he became rich thanks to Jacob, and said Jacob could pick his payment.

ideas.children_he: כְּדַאי לְהַסְכִּים מֵרֹאשׁ עַל שָׂכָר בָּרוּר.
ideas.children_en: Jacob said he wants only the spotted and special animals as his pay. This way everyone will know which animals are his to avoid arguments.

ideas.children_he: לָבָן נִסָּה לְשַׁנּוֹת אֶת הַמַּצָּב לְטוֹבָתוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Laban separated Jacob’s animals from his own to prevent more special animals being born and confusion, and moved them far apart.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב חִפֵּשׂ דֶּרֶךְ לְהַגְדִּיל אֶת עֶדְרָיו.
ideas.children_en: Jacob put special sticks in the water where the animals drank when they were ready to mate. This caused the animals to have spotted and striped young for his pay.
Jacob separated his best animals to breed and kept the weaker ones for Laban. He put sticks only when the strong animals were ready to mate.
Jacob became very successful with many animals. He also bought workers and camels and became the leader of a tribe.
